title: The Savoy Male and Female College
text:
[Photograph: A two-story wooden building with a bell tower or cupola at the top, decorated with ornamental trim. A sign on the building reads "Savoy Tea" or similar. Caption below the image is not fully legible.]

The building as actually erected was a two-story wooden structure of about six rooms, adorned at the top with a decorative belfry in the center (shown above).

In this belfry, later, was placed a bell purchased through the efforts of a group of students organizing themselves as "The Squintus Dramatic Club," a brief history of which appears in Part II, page 5, with a picture of the bell on page 14.

The bell (see picture on page —) contains an inscription reading as follows: "1901. Presented to Savoy College by Squintus Dramatic Club. E. K. Noseworthy (now deceased), Manager; Guy W. Thompson, now living at Dallas, Secretary; Prakney E. Durrett, now Mrs. W. H. Davis and living at Wichita Falls, Texas."

This bell is rung during each reunion of former students, but is not otherwise used by the present school.


EFFORTS TO REORGANIZE A COLLEGE
